newsitem.title: USA: DDL to acquire Century Electronics. [CORRECTED 17:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: DDL to acquire Century Electronics. [CORRECTED 17:15 GMT]

text.p: DDL Electronics Inc. said Friday it agreed to acquire Century Electronics Manufacturing Inc., a contract electronics maker based in Massachusetts, in a stock transaction worth about $50 million.

DDL, which provides manufacturing services for electronic equipment manufacturers, said it will exchange 33 million shares of its common stock to acquire 100 percent of Century, which is based in Southborough, Mass.

Based on DDL's trading price of $1.50 Friday, the deal would be worth about $49.5 million. As part of the deal, Century agreed to provide up $3.3 million to retire some of DDL's short-term debt (corrects to transpose companies).

Century, majority-owned by Centennial Technologies Inc., generated $24.6 million in revenue in the first quarter of this year. Combined, the two companies will generate $150 million in annual revenues, DDL said in a statement.
The merger, which is expected to close in September, is still subject to completing a definitive agreement and other conditions, DDL said. The merger will be accounted for as a purchase.
"We believe that this will be a highly synergistic merger because our two companies have complementary strengths and management teams," DDL Chief Executive Gregory Horton said in a statement.

In addition to providing manufacturing services, DDL, which is based in Newbury Park, Calif., also makes printed circuit boards for use in the computer, communications and electronic instrumentation industries.
